text:
alex: Heads up — I’m seeing a sudden spike in rate-limit errors and client 429s for a handful of customers. Started ~1783254110. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/rate-limiter/overview :warning:

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: rate-limiter-service v2 -> 10% traffic (canary-id: canary-20260315-01)

alex: Paging SRE oncall. Can we get eyes? Errors look like over-throttling, not increased traffic from clients.

ops-bot: @maria you have been paged for incident #INC-20260315-rl. SEV2. Pager ETA: 2m.

maria: On it — pulling logs now. Can you drop the sample request IDs?

alex: sample req ids: req_aa3b, req_7f2d, req_91c4. Customer reports timeouts and 429s intermittently.

maria: quick log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z rate-limiter.v2 token_check failure user_id=acct-987 code=THROTTLED exemptions_applied=0 tokens_remaining=5
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z rate-limiter.v2 token_check failure user_id=acct-123 code=THROTTLED exemptions_applied=0 tokens_remaining=0
```
This looks wrong — exemptions_applied should be >0 for internal/reserved accounts.

jordan: Pushed the v2 handler last hour. Canary should only affect 10%, but there was a routing config change earlier that expanded the canary group. Checking rollout config now.

deploy-bot: Rollout config change detected by audit: route-weight for region-us-west changed from 10% -> 100% at 1783254060 by ci/cd-pipeline. Trigger: automated canary promotion policy (BUG: promotion triggered without manual approval).

maria: Okay that explains full impact. Need immediate mitigation: either flip the new limiter off or apply hotfix to re-enable exemptions mapping.

jordan: We have a feature flag gate: rate_limiter_v2_enabled. I can toggle it. Command: `./ffctl set rate_limiter_v2_enabled false --env=prod --scope=global`

alex: If we toggle it, traffic will go back to v1. Any risk to token accounting or inconsistent token consumption?

jordan: v1 token accounting is stable. v2 introduced a header-name mapping bug — it reads `X-Client-Meta` instead of `x-customer-metadata` so exemptions lookup returns empty. Turning off v2 reverts to v1 behavior.

maria: Do it. Also add a temporary kill-switch at the gateway: `nginx: set rate_limit_by_lua_enabled off` for prod-edge to reduce pressure while we flip flags.

alex: @jordan go ahead. I’ll coordinate with on-call to watch dashboards.

jordan: Running ffctl now...

jordan: `> ./ffctl set rate_limiter_v2_enabled false --env=prod --scope=global`

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: rate_limiter_v2_enabled=false by jordan at 1783254221.

ops-bot: Executing gateway mitigation: set rate_limit_by_lua_enabled false on prod-edge nodes. Progress: 4/4 nodes updated.

maria: Traffic behavior improving. 429s down from 18% -> 1.8% in the last 60s. Continuing to monitor.

lia: Support update: we’ve opened tickets with top affected customers: acct-987, acct-123, acct-444. Liaison message drafted. Estimated MTTI ~10m.

kim: Need customer impact summary for comms. @lia can you add counts and percent of requests failed per customer?

lia: Sure — quick numbers: acct-987 saw 27% of requests 429 during the window, acct-123 14%, acct-444 9%. All in US-West.

maria: Can we rollback the canary promotion? If the promo automation promoted to 100% we should ensure the pipeline is reverted and the promotion policy fixed.

deploy-bot: Initiating rollback to rate-limiter-service v1 global at 1783254300. Job: rollback-20260315-rl-01.

jordan: Patch ready for v2: fix header key normalization in token-accounting module, add unit test for exemptions mapping, and add a canary guard to require manual approval for >20%. Will prepare PR and hotfix deploy after rollback.

maria: After rollback is confirmed, we should run a controlled canary with smoke checks: exemptions count > 0 for internal accounts and no increase in 429s after 10m.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete at 1783254332. Services back to v1. Health checks: pass.

alex: Confirming dashboards: 429 rate back to baseline ~0.2%. Great work.

jordan: Drafting PR now: https://git.redwood.internal/rate-limiter/pull/952 — includes mapping fix and stricter promotion rule. Will request review from maria and ops.

lia: Support comms — suggested message to customers: 
"We experienced elevated rate limit errors between 14:01–14:09 UTC due to an unintended canary promotion. The issue has been mitigated and service restored. We’re following up with a fix and will credit affected usage."

kim: @lia add estimated affected window and include the root cause summary (canary promotion automation + header mismatch). Also include support contact for escalation.

maria: Ops follow-up actions: 1) revert promotion automation config, 2) add canary approval gate >20%, 3) add monitoring alert on exemptions_applied == 0 for reserved accounts.

alex: Handoff — I’m stepping out in 30m; @maria will take extended watch until 18:00 UTC. Please escalate to jordan if new 429s spike.

maria: Taking watch. Added a temporary dashboard panel and an alert rule. If 429 > 1% sustained for 3m, page SRE/Eng.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-20260315-rl updated to status: mitigated. Postmortem requested within 48h. Assigned to jordan.

jordan: Will own postmortem and follow-up PR. Thanks everyone — I’ll include a timeline and the proposed release checklist change in the postmortem.

lia: Will send customer messages and log tickets for credits.

alex: Closing thread for now. Monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
